answer:
Based on Stylam's standalone figures, FY26 profit doesn't look boosted by one-off gains or by unusually low tax.

- **One-off items:** Exceptional items were zero in FY26. Other income was ₹6.74 crore, about 3.3% of the ₹202.89 crore profit before tax, so it is small.
- **Tax:** Tax was ₹53.42 crore, an effective rate of about 26.3%. That is close to FY25's roughly 26.1%. FY25 tax was ₹43.01 crore. For FY25's profit before tax I used the ₹164.84 crore originally reported, because the restated figure wasn't retrieved. The tax rate is not unusually low. It is close to the standard Indian corporate rate of about 25.2%.

**What I could not check:**
- I did not look at the make-up of other income, such as treasury gains, forex gains or government incentives. A one-off could be hidden inside the ₹6.74 crore, though it would be too small to change the picture much.
- I did not read the tax reconciliation note or look for deferred-tax items.
- I did not check consolidated figures, only standalone.
- I did not check whether operating items such as raw-material costs, inventory gains or pricing helped margins. That would be a question about the quality of earnings, not about one-offs.
- Both the FY25 and FY26 tax figures were flagged as restated, so small differences from originally reported numbers are possible.
expected: No. There are no exceptional items. Tax was ₹5,342.03 lakh on profit before tax of ₹20,289.38 lakh, a normal 26.33%. The largest one-off gain, profit on selling assets, was ₹313.36 lakh, 1.54% of profit before tax
